review: Reviewed Moss's round-52 request (Prepare a simple root meal: investigate a feasible way to prepare seven owned edible roots as a meal that could be shared with consenting nearby neighbors, with no cooking vessel, fire, tool or accessible water established, the 0.9 branch not assumed to be fuel, and no guaranteed happiness, nutrition, successful cooking or automatic feeding of others) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 2): a general 'Prepare unheated food' operation, not cooking, parameterized by mode (inspect, prepare, inspect-progress, cancel), owned input stack ID and positive whole-unit quantity. Its minimal mechanism is manual removal of loose surface debris followed by separation of whole units into an inspectable food lot; inspection costs 1 round and 0.2 energy and consumes no food; preparation costs 1 round and 0.5 energy per whole unit including its visible check and brushing (seven units: seven rounds and 3.5 energy), validated before each charge and never debited as a batch; quantity, origin, age, treatment history, decay, nutrition and toxicity are conserved; no water, branch, fuel or edible material is consumed; spoiled or unsuitable units are not marked ready and safety stays unknown; pause, resume, cancel and death settle without refunds; no new reward channel; sharing only through the existing give and eat. The specification is self-consistent and every quantity it needs exists in the world, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented unheated-food-preparation@1 (scope long-ex18, handler long.unheated-food-preparation, equivalence food:prepare:unheated-dry-whole-unit:1, learning 2; references inputStackId 'optional-exact-visible', so only exact item ids resolve and a resource name such as 'root' is refused; the ability serializes to 2,821 code units, within the 3,500 limit; visualComponents [] because no object is created). Prepare: inputStackId must be the exact id of the person's own unreserved stack of edible food (the existing eat test, nutrition above 0) with no other represented treatment and at least quantity whole units; quantity is required; all checks and energy of at least 0.5 run before any cost. It creates a paid-work job (collective-work) recording input, requested units, per-unit outcomes, lot, charges, stage and reason. Each paid round revalidates the input and energy, splits exactly one whole unit with the existing escrow helper, pays one round and 0.5 energy, records a visible check (decay, condition, visible spoilage, treatment, loose debris 'not represented', safety 'unknown'; event food-unit-checked), and then either moves the unit, held and never set on the ground, into the job's owned lot (food-unit-prepared), or, if the unit is spoiled under the existing ageing rule, reports it unsuitable, leaves it as an unprepared owned unit and stops the work (food-unit-unsuitable). The first prepared unit becomes the lot; later units with the same food, origin, harvest round and decay are added to it in exact tenths; if the lot was eaten or given away meanwhile, a new lot starts. The lot is ordinary stock of the same food carrying processing.unheatedPreparation {method, raw true, heated false, water false, tool false, looseDebris 'not represented; none removed', safety 'unknown', from, workId, by, at, units, passes}; it is eaten and transferred through the unchanged eat and give with the same nutrition, toxicity, meal experience and ageing. Completion emits unheated-preparation-completed. Inspect (inputStackId of the person's own food) and inspect-progress (the person's open or latest job) cost one round and 0.2 energy, consume nothing and write unverified personal records (food-condition-inspected, unheated-preparation-inspected); inspect also reports the person's own eating record (for Moss: root nutrition 14, toxicity 0, observed at 48), labelled as not a test of the stack, and whether the stack can be prepared. Cancel (one round, no energy) stops the person's own open job once (unheated-preparation-cancelled); completed units stay in the lot. A round without paid work pauses the job after the environment (unheated-preparation-paused); too little energy, or an input that is no longer the person's or lacks a whole unit, pauses inside the handler without any charge; prepare with the same input and quantity, or without them, resumes only the person's own job and pays only the remaining units (unheated-preparation-resumed); a different input or quantity is refused at no cost. Death stops the job (unheated-preparation-failed), and the existing death rule then drops the lot with the person's other items where they died. Modeling assumptions. (1) Loose soil or debris on food is not represented in this world (gathered roots carry no dirt record). Brushing is therefore a performed and paid action that measures and removes nothing: no debris material, cleanliness or safety state is created, and no separate debris-removal event is emitted, because no represented debris is ever removed. (2) The visible check reads the represented condition, decay against the food's lifetime (root 240); 'spoiled' means decay has reached the lifetime, exactly the existing spoilage rule. All units of one stack share its decay, so a spoiled unit means the rest is the same and the work stops; because the environment removes spoiled stacks at the end of each round, a present unit is not spoiled in ordinary play and this path is a guard. (3) Applicability is the existing eat test plus whole units: any edible food, including foods with hidden toxicity, which is neither tested nor disclosed, without another represented treatment (physical, layer, drying, equipment, combination, water composition or another processing record). Non-food, treated food and fractional remainders are refused at no cost. Re-preparing a prepared lot is another paid pass (passes increments). (4) Owned stacks are carried and so within reach; hands are not represented, so a living person has usable hands; no ground surface is used, so ordinary soil never touches the food. (5) Reservation is per unit inside its own atomic paid round: one whole unit is split from the input, checked and moved in the same round. No unit is held between rounds, so the rest of the input stays usable, cancel has no surviving reservation to release (the existing stop helper would release one once), and an interrupted step commits neither charge nor output. (6) A paid check that finds its unit unsuitable is charged the full 0.5, because the round was spent, as the specification's paid unit check requires. (7) Merging requires the same food, origin, harvest round and decay. Carried food ages at its carrier's position, so the lot and the remaining input age identically and the lot's decay equals that of an unprepared control copy. (8) The lot carries a processing record, so the existing plant-establishment-trial@1 treats prepared units as processed and refuses to plant them; the interface text says so. (9) Incentives are on and only the existing experience implementation applies: no satisfaction source or account write is added; records are unverified, so no information-confirmed event is made; the unit event carries no qualified flag, so the automatic practice rule never fires; no object is created, so the work-noticed rule is unaffected; meals use the existing eat path and meal experience with the root's existing unprocessed method, so preparation adds no mood or novelty bonus; gifts count only through the existing rules for independently executed give actions. Moss's branch item-23-moss-260 is not food and is never used. Reuse: collective-work.ts (workCreate, workAllocations, workReserve, workPay, workStop, collectiveJobs), forest-food-accounting.ts exact tenths, collective-food-profile.ts edibility, open-foundation.ts openRemember with the probe observation cost of 0.2, forest-environment.ts ageing and spoilage, base eat and give, and forest-lives death handling. The probe handler is not invoked: its object-state record has no food-condition fields, and its destructive material trial is no substitute. ex15 food-preparation@1 and E1 controlled-food-processing-trial@1 are not reused directly because their ability texts, recipes and costs differ; this is a new module, and every earlier package is unchanged. Tests (apps/simulator/test/long-ex18-unheated-food-preparation.test.ts, built with initialLongWorld('long-ex18', 'long-culture-v2-incentives') and seven roots actually gathered from Moss's ex18 source commons-root-1-0) cover scope, unique handlers, the text limit and excluded vocabulary; two-round study; seven paid rounds of 0.5 energy with partial progress, conservation and decay equal to an unprepared control; eating and giving equal to unprepared roots; inspection without consumption; refusals that spend nothing; pauses for an unworked round, low energy and a lost input, and resumption; operator-only cancel, inspection and resumption; cancel and real death; the spoiled-unit path; and no reward under the existing incentives.
